subject: AcmeCloud private deployment: data map & egress next steps
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-27T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: AcmeCloud private deployment: data map & egress next steps

Hi Sofia — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the concrete asks we captured on our side so we can align engineering: 

Call recap (high level):
- Scope: Private/VPC deployment of Redwood inference (customer-managed VPC + Redwood private control plane).
- Concern areas: PII mapping, retention requirements, logging/audit trails, network boundary constraints (no outbound internet for inference hosts), and where an on-prem or air-gapped connector may be needed.

Open items for Acme that will drive our design:
1) Data origins: Which systems will send data to Redwood (e.g., application API, batch SFTP, on-prem DB replicator)? For each, please indicate whether payloads include PII (email, name, account id, billing identifiers).
2) Retention windows: Desired retention for inference inputs, outputs, and logs (audit logs / request metadata). Are there different retention policies for billing vs. support vs. legal holds?
3) Egress policy: Can outbound traffic be restricted to a small set of IPs/hostnames? Are NAT / proxy-only egress patterns acceptable, or do you require fully air-gapped (no internet)?
4) Residency: Must logs and any persisted data remain in-region (us-east-1) or on-prem?
5) KMS/HSM: Do you require integration with your customer-managed KMS or HSM for key wrapping/CEKs?

Next steps we propose:
- Sofia / IT-Security: share a simple system/dataflow diagram + ACLs that show where PII originates and any existing on-prem connectors (SFTP, Kafka, DB replicas).
- Acme: share retention policy excerpts (can be a short table).
- Redwood: we will produce a proposed dataflow diagram for the private deployment (network boundaries + egress options) and a short matrix mapping each data type to retention & logging controls.

If you can send the diagram and the security requirements spreadsheet, we’ll circulate an internal pre-read and set a technical handoff with infra owners. Proposed 60-min slot: Thu 2026-06-03 10:00 ET — does that work for your team?

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment references: post-call notes (we'll attach Redwood-side notes once consolidated).

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia@acmecloud.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: IT Security <itsecurity@acmecloud.com>, legal@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-05-28T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmeCloud private deployment: data map & egress next steps

Diego — thanks for the clear recap. Strong alignment on our side; attaching a short diagram and the security requirements spreadsheet to answer your specific items. Quick answers inline: 

1) Data origins: primary sources are:
   - Application API (real-time requests) — includes account_id, user_email, free-text fields (PII present).
   - Billing exports (nightly) — customer billing identifiers, no free-text PII.
   - On-prem analytics DB (replicated) — may contain user identifiers; replication via an outbound VPN.

2) Retention: we have different windows: billing = 7 years, application logs (request-level) = 90 days, aggregated metrics = 2 years. Legal holds will require preservation beyond primary retention windows.

3) Egress: We cannot allow arbitrary outbound internet from production VPCs. Approved patterns:
   - Egress to specific partner IPs and ports (we can provide allowlist).
   - Relay/proxy inside our VPC is acceptable (Redwood may connect to an internal relay endpoint).
   - Fully air-gapped (no internet) for a subset of workloads is possible but adds operational overhead.

4) Residency: All persisted logs and request metadata must reside in our us-east-1 tenancy. Backups to other regions are not permitted.

5) KMS: We need Redwood to support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS with key policies that allow Redwood role access (we'll provide the key ARN).

Please find attached: acme-dataflow-20260528.pdf (diagram), security-reqs.xlsx (short matrix). Let us know if you need a packet capture or specific VPC CIDRs — we can provide during the technical handoff.

We can do Thu 2026-06-03 10:00 ET. I'll loop in our infra lead once we confirm.

—Sofia Ramos
Head of Product Security, AcmeCloud

Attachments: acme-dataflow-20260528.pdf (diagram), security-reqs.xlsx (matrix)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-29T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmeCloud private deployment: data map & egress next steps

Thanks Diego — tagging internal owners. Notes from Sofia's reply:
- PII present in app API and on-prem DB replication; billing retention = 7 years; request logs = 90 days; residency required us-east-1; allowlist-only egress or internal relay accepted; KMS required.

Immediate asks for us before the handoff: 
- Ben: validate feasibility of relay-only egress and whether we can support an in-VPC relay endpoint that eliminates outbound internet need for inference hosts. Also check whether S3 logging with lifecycle can satisfy 90-day retention and legal hold snapshot needs.
- Rafael: pricing impact for an air-gapped / relay architecture (extra infra + support overhead) — rough order of magnitude to share during next touch.
- Diego: prepare the initial Redwood dataflow diagram showing control plane (private), inference hosts, KV cache behavior, and where logs persist (we should annotate which data is encrypted by customer KMS).

I'll spin up a short meeting invite for 2026-06-03 10:00 ET and include our infra and product security. We should come with a proposed network egress matrix and two recommended deployment patterns (relay-only vs. limited-egress).

Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-31T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AcmeCloud private deployment: data map & egress next steps

Sofia — thanks for the detailed matrix and the diagram (appreciate the clarity). A few technical clarifications and our proposed options: 

1) Relay-only egress: feasible. We can deploy a lightweight proxy/relay inside your VPC (AMI/container) that accepts inference traffic from your private subnets and forwards to Redwood via a customer-managed NAT/peering that only allows traffic to our ingress endpoint. That eliminates outbound internet from the inference hosts.

2) No-internet / air-gap: we support a strictly air-gapped pattern via on-prem connectors (for batch workflows) and a hybrid model for real-time where the relay runs on-prem and communicates over a dedicated VPN. This increases operational complexity and will likely raise cost.

3) Logging & retention: request logs can be written to your S3 in us-east-1. We support writing structured audit logs with configurable TTL; lifecycle rules + object lock can satisfy the 90-day window and legal holds. We will always encrypt at rest with customer KMS if you provide the ARN.

4) CIDR / allowlist: to proceed we need an allowlist of the subnets that will host the relay and the NAT endpoints you plan to use. We can also publish a short set of egress endpoints if you prefer Redwood-initiated connections to a relay.

Attached is a short options doc: redwood-egress-options.pdf — it sketches the two deployment patterns and the operational tradeoffs.

I'll plan to be on the handoff call on 2026-06-03 10:00 ET. Proposed agenda for that call: 1) confirm in-scope data sources, 2) review acme-dataflow diagram and map fields to retention, 3) pick a deployment pattern (relay-only vs hybrid), 4) identify infra owners and timeline.

Ben Carter
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
